summary: Endpoint beaconing to a rare external domain after a user opened a macro-enabled attachment.
evidence: Office process spawned a scripting interpreter
Periodic outbound connections every 60s to a newly registered domain
investigation: Endpoint activity showed scheduled task and encoded script execution
outcome: Malware removed, but volatile memory artifacts were lost, so the payload family and any credential theft could not be confirmed.
analyst_feedback: Isolation was right but we should have captured a memory and triage snapshot first, or at least checked whether the host held cached credentials.
lessons_learned: Capture memory/triage data before isolating or re-imaging a compromised endpoint
Assume credentials cached on a compromised host may be stolen and review that user's logins
detection_gaps: Macro-enabled attachments from external senders were not sandboxed
